status_note: Art. 6 amended only by new paras 1a-1c per 2026/1744 point (8); Art. 6(1)(a)-(b) wording itself not seen officially (original OJ page extraction stops at recital 104).
requirement_paraphrase: An AI system is high-risk if it is a safety component of, or is itself, a product covered by Annex I legislation AND that product must undergo third-party conformity assessment under that legislation.
applies_to: Robots, drones, machines whose AI is a safety component of an Annex I product requiring third-party assessment

edition_or_version: AI Act Art. 60 as shown on unofficial reproduction; text version/amendment level not confirmed
status_note: Official: Art. 60(1)-(2) replaced by point (24): now covers Annex III and Annex I Section A systems; new Art. 60a for Section B products. The 30 day tacit approval and six month limit were not read officially.
requirement_paraphrase: Real-world testing of high-risk AI outside sandboxes requires a testing plan, market-surveillance approval (tacit after 30 days unless national law differs), registration, max about six months (one extension), informed consent, and reversibility of AI outputs; serious incidents go through Art 73.
applies_to: Providers testing high-risk AI in real conditions

status_note: Art. 72(3) replaced by 2026/1744 point (30): plan is part of Annex IV documentation; Commission guidance and template by 2 Sep 2027.
requirement_paraphrase: Providers must run a documented post-market monitoring system, collecting and analysing performance data over the system lifetime, with a plan included in Annex IV documentation; Annex I Section A providers may merge it into existing monitoring.

status_note: In force; high-risk obligations apply per B17
requirement_paraphrase: Serious incidents must be reported to the market surveillance authority no later than 15 days after awareness; 2 days for widespread infringements; 10 days for deaths; provider must investigate and not alter the system in ways that hamper cause analysis without telling authorities.
applies_to: High-risk AI system providers (and deployers where applicable)

edition_or_version: As published; applicability dates per site
requirement_paraphrase: Providers of high-risk AI systems must report serious incidents to market surveillance authorities: no later than 15 days after awareness (immediately once causal link established), 2 days for widespread infringements, 10 days for deaths; must investigate and not alter the system before informing authorities.
applies_to: Providers of high-risk AI systems (Annex I/III)

status_note: In force; high-risk obligations apply per B17
requirement_paraphrase: Provider must run a documented, lifecycle risk management system: identify and estimate risks from intended use and foreseeable misuse, assess post-market risks, adopt targeted measures; test against predefined metrics and thresholds before placing on market; consider under-18s.
applies_to: High-risk AI systems (incl. Annex I robots/drones where Art. 6(1) is met)

requirement_paraphrase: Testing must use metrics and probabilistic thresholds defined in advance and suited to the intended purpose; testing may include real-world testing, which must meet Art 57 or 60 conditions; testing is done throughout development and in any event before placing on the market or putting into service.

instrument: Willers et al., deep learning safety concerns in perception
requirement_paraphrase: Paper aims to list technical safety concerns of deep learning in perception for robots, drones and vehicles and mitigations, and to identify missing mitigations.
applies_to: Deep learning perception in autonomous agents

edition_or_version: Guidance (arXiv 2102.01564, 2021); York page: brochure dated Oct 2025
requirement_paraphrase: Six-stage process producing artefacts and a GSN argument per stage: ML safety assurance scoping; ML safety requirements; data management (relevance, completeness, accuracy, balance requirements; dev/test/verification datasets); model learning; model verification (test or formal, independent of development).
applies_to: Autonomous systems with ML components (incl. robots)

requirement_paraphrase: Deployment stage: integrate model, record and monitor development assumptions, monitor inputs against training distribution, log erroneous behaviour, test integration (simulation, HIL, shadow, controlled real-world, with evidence simulator represents reality), and argue an integration claim and an operation claim.

instrument: AMLAS Guidance on Assurance of ML in Autonomous Systems
status_note: Open guidance from University of York
clause_or_section_seen: Six stages: scoping, ML safety requirements, data management, model learning, model verification, deployment
requirement_paraphrase: Process plus GSN argument patterns for ML components; top claim that the ML component meets allocated safety requirements in the defined environment; verification by test and/or formal methods using independent verification data.
applies_to: ML components (mainly offline supervised) in autonomous systems

instrument: AMLAS Guidance on Assurance of ML in Autonomous Systems
requirement_paraphrase: Data requirements must be justified (data requirements justification report) and datasets checked for relevance, completeness, accuracy and balance; environment description must be explicit.

instrument: Safety Case Templates for Autonomous Systems (Adelard, for Dstl)
requirement_paraphrase: Argument templates for ML-enabled autonomy: requirements, hazard analysis (ODD structures scenarios), safety monitor architecture, ML-based sensor, adaptation over time, plus defeaters and evidence confidence.

instrument: Safety Assurance Argument Templates for Autonomous Systems (Adelard for Dstl)
clause_or_section_seen: Sections 5-10 (requirements, hazard analysis, safety monitor with ML, ML sensor, performance, adaptation)
requirement_paraphrase: Provides argument templates incl. a safety-monitor architecture with environmental, health and behaviour guards, and ML-sensor arguments with confidence from real and simulated trials (headings seen); hazard analysis section suggests ODD validity/completeness could be assessed separately from hazard analysis of the intended function.

instrument: Hoss, Scholtes, Eckstein - Review of Testing Object-Based Environment Perception
clause_or_section_seen: Review sections on ODD coverage, sensor limits, datasets
requirement_paraphrase: Notes that covering the ODD with test scenarios is hard, public datasets target diversity not safety relevance, simulation struggles to model sensor-environment interaction, and RTK-GNSS reference accuracy degrades near buildings/trees.

instrument: Adee et al. - Discovery of Perception Performance Limiting Triggering Conditions
requirement_paraphrase: Proposes a Bayesian-network method to find perception triggering conditions; states SOTIF gives no concrete method for identifying new triggering conditions.
